transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Lee, I came in because... well, I've been noticing some things lately. The men I play dominoes with, they say things. Just little messages, you know? And sometimes the announcer on the radio does it too. It's meant for me. My wife, she tells me it's just regular talk, but... I know what I'm hearing. They're warning me. Telling me I need to be careful.
Can you tell me how long you've been noticing these messages and warnings from the men and the radio announcer?
Well, I'd say... it's been about nine months now. They come and go, you know, just on and off. But the voices and those special messages, they started up right around nine months ago.
During these past nine months, have you noticed any periods where your mood was very low, very high, or unusually irritable, separate from the messages you've been hearing?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. There are weeks where I wake up just feeling... well, real bright and important. I'll be laughing loud and talking real fast about things. But the thing is, if my wife or somebody tries to slow me down, or if they question what I'm doing, I get pretty sharp with them. I just get easily bothered by it.
Do you notice these special messages and warnings from the men or the radio even during times when you're not feeling unusually high-energy or irritable—like when your mood feels pretty normal?

Yes, I do. Actually, there was... well, a quiet spell a while back. Maybe for a whole month, I was just feeling regular. I was sleeping fine, not having any of those big ideas or getting worked up. But even then... I still heard my friend talking out on the porch when nobody was there. And I still knew the radio was sending those messages right to me. So it doesn't seem to matter how I'm feeling, they just keep coming.
Over these past nine months, would you say the times when you felt unusually high, irritable, or low made up most of that time, or were they just brief periods compared to the rest?

Well, if I look back over the whole nine months... I'd have to say the high spells, and the time it takes to settle down from them, have taken up the majority of it. There were definitely more months filled with that high energy and being irritable than there were calm stretches.

latest_inference.note: Mood (manic-like) episodes have dominated the 9-month course, but psychotic symptoms (referential auditory hallucinations, delusions) persisted for about a month with no mood disturbance, confirming psychosis independent of mood episodes. This pattern—mood symptoms present for the majority of the illness duration plus a distinct psychotic-only period—fits schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, ruling out schizophrenia (F20.9) and narrowing from unspecified schizoaffective disorder (F25.9) to the bipolar subtype (F25.0).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, delusions of reference) spanning 9 months, concurrent with manic-like mood episodes (elevated mood, grandiosity, pressured speech, irritability) that occupy the majority of the illness duration. Critically, there was a distinct ~1-month period where psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, delusions of reference) persisted in the absence of any mood symptoms, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring independent of mood disturbance. Since mood symptoms (manic type) were present for the majority of the total illness duration and psychotic symptoms occurred both during and independent of mood episodes, this meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than primary psychotic disorder (F20.9) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (F31.2).
